faq.a: Yasin is associated with the Arabic form يَاسِين, whose core sense is yasin; ya-sin (a quranic surah name).

faq.q: What is the origin of Yasin?
faq.a: Yasin is associated with Arabic. Yasin is Arabic يَاسِين (Yāsīn), the name of a surah of the Quran.
Yes — the underlying form يَاسِين is Arabic.
Yasin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yasin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yāsīn occurs in the Quran as the name of a surah and a Quranic form.

faq.q: What does Yasin mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Yasin is rendered یاسین and carries the sense یاسین، قرآن کی سورت.

faq.q: What does Yasin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Yasin is rendered یاسین and carries the sense یاسین، نام سوره قرآن.
A romanized syllable approximation is ya-sin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Yasin?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Yasin, yasin. Script forms are يَاسِين, یاسین, यासीन.

faq.q: Is Yasin a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
